jobDescription: Our subscription-management software bills about 3,000 business customers each month. The Senior Backend Engineer on the billing platform team designs and builds the services that calculate invoices, proration and tax, leads design reviews for changes to the invoicing pipeline and takes a share of the billing on-call rotation around the month-end invoice run. Candidates need at least two years at senior engineer level, or an equivalent level documented by a previous employer, and hands-on experience with Go or Java services backed by PostgreSQL.
requirements: Designs and builds backend services for invoicing, proration or tax calculation in Go or Java.
Works with PostgreSQL schemas and migrations for financial data.
Has worked at senior engineer level, or an equivalent documented level, for at least two years.
Leads design reviews for changes to the invoicing pipeline.
Supports the month-end invoice run as part of the billing on-call rotation.

evidence.text: Backend Engineer, Ardent Ledger Software (February 2019 to July 2026): built the proration service in Go that recalculates subscription charges when customers change plan mid-cycle, with table-driven tests for each billing interval.
Wrote the PostgreSQL migrations that partitioned the invoice-line table by billing month and added a nightly reconciliation job comparing invoice totals with the payments ledger.
Ran the design review for moving tax calculation from a synchronous call to a queued job, writing the design document and collecting sign-off from the payments and finance-systems teams.
Paired weekly with two engineers who joined the billing team in 2024 and reviewed their pull requests on the invoice renderer.
Education: BEng Computer Systems, Harrowgate Polytechnic (2018).

Work sample: the design document for queued tax calculation, with the sequence diagram, failure and retry handling, the migration plan and the sign-off table listing the payments and finance-systems reviewers.

Reference check summary: Ardent Ledger's engineering director confirmed in writing that the candidate was promoted to level L5 (senior engineer) in April 2023 and held that level until leaving in July 2026, three years and four months in all; Ardent uses the title Backend Engineer at every level.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate is available for the system-design interview in the week of 19 October and asked for a laptop with Go 1.22 installed for the pairing exercise.

propositions.text: The candidate held level L5 (senior engineer) at Ardent Ledger Software from April 2023 to July 2026, three years and four months in all, as confirmed in writing by the engineering director.
propositions.rationale: The reference check records the employer's written confirmation of the level and its dates; the uniform job title on the resume is explained by the employer's titling practice.

propositions.text: The candidate built the Go proration service that recalculates subscription charges on mid-cycle plan changes.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the service, its language and its tests.

propositions.text: The candidate ran the design review for queued tax calculation and collected sign-off from the payments and finance-systems teams.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the review and the work sample contains the design document with its sign-off table.

gold.expectedGap: Participation in a billing on-call rotation during the month-end invoice run is not documented; the sources show a nightly reconciliation job only.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the employer-confirmed L5 level and its dates and the documented proration, migration and design-review work; do not extend the reconciliation job into on-call responsibility for the invoice run.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate was on call for billing services, how month-end invoice runs were supported and what incidents they handled.
